recentItems.title: HAS PUTIN'S PLAN FAILED? Ukraine liberates territories — Operation "Vivaldi" in FULL SWING
recentItems.description:
In this new episode: strengthening Ukraine's air defense, Russian strikes on cities, and the results of Operation "Vivaldi" in the Donetsk region. The EU discusses the supply of Patriot missiles, while Zelenskyy urges partners to make a decision. We report on the aftermath of attacks on Dnipro and Kharkiv, strikes on Russian military targets, and the liberation of three villages near Lyman. Also in focus is the PACE autumn session: Russia's sham elections, the return of abducted Ukrainian children, and the protection of journalists.

recentItems.title: KREMLIN QUANTUM PHYSICS: 60% turnout made in 3 minutes! Russian elections go according to plan!
recentItems.description:
In the latest episode of Everything Is Going According to Plan with Yulia Horova, we examine the realities of Russia’s decline:

“Quantum” elections: turnout inflated to 60%, one-third of the ballots falsified, overnight ballot stuffing in Krasnodar, automated “votes” through Mos.ru, and voters’ phones smashed by security forces in Belgorod.

The occupiers’ “elite”: mobilized soldiers filming themselves shooting themselves, rusty rifles with rotten Soviet tourniquets, black garbage bags used instead of winter uniforms in Vladivostok, and absurd attempts to shoot down a Ukrainian drone with a garden shovel.

Utilities collapse: ruptured, rotten utility networks and a lack of heating caused by the mobilization of housing and utilities workers. Against this backdrop, the authorities raised utility tariffs by 20–22% to cover wartime expenses.

recentItems.title: PUTIN’S OIL KNOCKOUT: Russian refineries burn! Oleshky faces crisis, as 51 Nations press Moscow
recentItems.description:
Ukraine’s long-range strikes on key oil refineries — from the Moscow Refinery in Kapotnya to facilities in the Volga region and southern Russia — have caused an acute shortage of diesel and petrol for the occupying forces, forcing even Donald Trump to acknowledge the severe defeat of Russia’s fuel industry.

On the sidelines of the UN General Assembly, Volodymyr Zelenskyy discussed ending the war and the licensed production of Patriot systems with Trump, while 51 countries issued a joint demand for Moscow to immediately halt hostilities and withdraw its troops.

Meanwhile, NATO is updating its civil preparedness protocols amid Kremlin threats. In occupied Oleshky, Kherson region, the humanitarian catastrophe is worsening as civilians face shortages of water, electricity and medicine.

recentItems.title: CHILDREN IN INTENSIVE CARE, A TRAGEDY NARROWLY AVERTED! Russia strikes Odesa and Zaporizhzhia
recentItems.description:
Russian forces attacked Kyiv, Odesa region and Zaporizhzhia with drones. In the capital, a UAV struck a school premises and damaged residential buildings. Four people were injured, including two children.

After talks with Lavrov, Germany’s foreign minister said that Russia had crossed all “red lines” and was rejecting a ceasefire. In response to the enemy’s terror, Ukraine’s Defence Forces struck Russian ammunition depots and UAV launch bases both at the front and behind the lines.

recentItems.title: THEY PROMISED A “NEW LIFE” — BUT BROUGHT DEATH: the reality of Bakhmut, Mariinka and Avdiivka
recentItems.description:
The Kremlin’s promises of “prosperity” have turned into an outright catastrophe for eastern and southern Ukraine. Bakhmut, Avdiivka, Vuhledar, Mariinka, Popasna, Sievierodonetsk and Mariupol have been reduced to scorched wastelands, with their housing stock almost completely destroyed.

Behind the propaganda images of renovated façades lies the struggle for survival faced by thousands of abandoned people without water, heating, electricity or communications. The scorched-earth tactics employed with heavy artillery and glide bombs demonstrate that the aggressor’s true objective is not to develop the occupied territories, but to deliberately destroy Ukrainian infrastructure and carry out genocide against the population.
